description:
Root-cause spike complete. The dirty retry prototype is not a landing candidate: it reconstructs callable and carrier authority downstream, which is why the continuation symptom remains.

Output contract
A first-class callable value has one immutable construction-owned runtime boundary. It carries actual semantic captures, explicit physical capture slots, its producer-correlated resolved member set, a uniform boxed closure-call ABI, and a boxed return seam. Member-specific dispatch, target ABI decoding, and return reconstruction occur only inside that boundary. DispatchSet/callable-wide inventory remains analysis only.

First losses
1. Backend rediscovers a FunctionRef/Lambda through CallableId, expands callable-wide members, and invents capture ordinal -> target-input-prefix mappings, discarding CallableFlowFact authority.
2. Bare Position -> ShapeId conflates structural payload layout with non-structural runtime carriage. Nothing means structural zero width, not semantic absence.
3. transport_slot conflates logical position with physical closure slot; native reads position presence as physical presence.
4. Native/codegen reselect members.first() after wrapper construction, restoring arbitrary target ABI.

Required model
Transport publishes TransportLayout { structural: ShapeId, carrier: Absent | ValueRef } from runtime-demand endpoints (EntryCapture and ClosureCall callee) and role-bearing incoming edges (CallableCapture; ordinary direct edges forward only). ShapeDescr remains structural-only. Carrier is NOT a generic executable-input ABI lane: a full-lib probe proved that widening target parameters breaks direct-call ABI. Carrier is consumed only when projecting a CallableFlowFact construction into explicit physical closure/capture slots and its member semantic-role mappings. Direct executable ABI remains structural.

Construction is keyed by producer Value position and owns actual captures, physical slots from TransportLayout, resolved members, uniform wrapper call ABI, and boxed return. Backend maps symbols to targets once; native/interpreter/codegen consume this construction contract. The wrapper alone adapts members.

Delete rather than compensate
Remove post-hoc carrier scans/forced value-lane rewrites, construction/ingress ABI rediscovery, transport_slot-as-presence, CallableId/position entry selection, generic carrier-to-param injection, and legacy singleton member ABI fields.

Proof
Use fixtures2/00181_enum_reduce_operator_ref.fz plus enum_predicate_search, enum_take_drop_split, range-reduce scalar, and a heterogeneous-member construction test. Assert artifacts expose construction slot ownership separately from structural layout; run interpreter and JIT paths. Lazy sid22 descriptor tagging is confirmed correct and is not the first loss.

Wrapper lowering discovery
The existing native callable boundary is a one-target Cranelift shim and the interpreter identity table is likewise identity -> one BackendCallableEntry.target. A construction with multiple resolved members therefore cannot be represented by callable-entry identity, nor can native-only lookup replacement fix it. Publish BackendConstructionWrapper with dense construction identity, the construction-owned boxed capture/call/return ABI, and member adapters paired with the already-settled semantic dispatch plan. Lower that single artifact in both interpreter and native; it alone selects a member and decodes/reconstructs its ABI. Do not choose members.first(), re-derive a target from CallableId/position, or inject carrier lanes into executable ABI.
title: fz-k22: shared consumer bodies must dispatch closure calls through the VALUE-carried entry identity -- a static position->entry stamp is unrepresentable for type-variable arg slots
